The United States has been conducting presidential elections for 232 years. No modern candidate has ever refused to accept the results and recognize the winner’s legitimacy.

When that happens, the 2020 election, conducted in the midst of a pandemic, with by far the most votes ever cast, will be over. And despite Trump’s refusal to concede, there is every indication that it was run honestly and the results tabulated accurately — a tribute to the professionalism and integrity of officials across the country.
Before Election Day, the Trump administration invited a delegation of 28 international experts from the Organization of American States, which has reported on elections around the world, to observe the vote. Its preliminary report found zero evidence of significant fraud.
Last month, the New York Times spoke to top election officials in 49 of 50 states. Not one, Democrat or Republican, reported “that fraud or other irregularities played a role in the outcome of the presidential race.”
On Nov. 12, the coordinating council overseeing the voting systems used around the country said in an unprecedented statement distributed by Trump’s own Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) that “the November 3rd election was the most secure in American history” and that “there is no evidence that any voting system deleted or lost votes, changed votes, or was in any way compromised.”

Unwilling to disenfranchise millions of voters and reverse the results of the presidential election, the U.S. Supreme Court refused on Friday to hear a flimsy lawsuit that Texas sought to file against Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan and Georgia, effectively exhausting Trump’s legal options.

The clearest message is that 2020 contained ordinary errors and isolated misconduct, but no evidence of coordinated fraud capable of changing the presidential result. [shard_05694_59439] [shard_02831_27781]

Claims about dead voters, double voting, and illegal ballots were often based on outdated registration records, mistaken identities, legally cast ballots, or unverified allegations, while reviews found fewer than 475 potential fraud cases across six contested states and no coordinated scheme. [shard_02831_27781]

That does not mean fraud is impossible; it means the documented cases were too few and too small to support the claim that the election was stolen. [shard_02831_27781]

The Dominion claim should be explained through Antrim County, Michigan, where inaccurate unofficial results resulted from human errors involving last-minute ballot changes, and hand counting the paper ballots plus a statewide risk-limiting audit confirmed the corrected outcome. [shard_06032_25201]

Election-security officials likewise reported no evidence that voting systems deleted, lost, or changed votes, although isolated glitches and data-entry mistakes did occur and should be corrected transparently rather than dismissed. [shard_05694_59439]

The “blocked poll watchers” story in Fulton County, Georgia, conflated different stages of mail-ballot processing: some workers and observers left after one task ended, but state officials said counting continued under observation and found no suitcases of illegal ballots. [shard_05694_59439]

Mail voting is not simply “unchecked voting,” because jurisdictions use voter-registration records, signature or identity checks, ballot accounting, secure storage, and other procedures that vary by state. [shard_02831_27781]

A ballot being mailed to an address, collected after Election Day, or deposited by someone other than the voter does not by itself prove fraud, because ballots are generally valid according to when and how they were submitted and some states legally authorize designated agents or ballot collection. [shard_02831_27781] [shard_01855_19144]

The “2000 Mules” allegations went beyond the evidence: the film did not establish that the supposedly tracked ballots were fraudulent, its cellphone-location precision claims were unreliable, and repeated proximity to drop boxes or nonprofit offices could have innocent explanations. [shard_01855_19144]

Arizona’s partisan-led Maricopa County review is especially useful for a bipartisan forum because, despite its expansive fraud allegations and controversial methods, its own reported hand count increased Biden’s total by 99 votes and reduced Trump’s by 261, thereby confirming Biden’s victory. [shard_04324_25248]

Residents should distinguish three questions that are often collapsed into one: whether a rule was followed, whether an administrative mistake occurred, and whether the mistake changed the result. [shard_06032_25201] [shard_02831_27781]

The most confidence-building safeguards are voter-marked paper ballots, secure and publicly documented chain of custody, bipartisan or otherwise credibly independent observation, routine risk-limiting audits, recount procedures triggered by meaningful discrepancies, and prompt publication of canvass and audit data. [shard_03394_71131] [shard_06032_25201]

Paper ballots alone are not a magic solution, because their value depends on transparent custody, accurate reconciliation, competent staff, and audits that can detect and investigate discrepancies. [shard_03394_71131]

Ballot tracking, clear cure procedures for correctable mail-ballot problems, accessible drop-off arrangements, and well-trained observers can improve both security and the voter’s ability to see that the ballot entered the system. [shard_02831_27781] [shard_04372_71246]

Every proposed integrity law should therefore be tested against both sides of the objective: does it address a documented vulnerability, and does it impose avoidable burdens on elderly, disabled, rural, working, or otherwise less-mobile voters. [shard_01855_19144] [shard_01384_44316]

[shard_04372_71246] [shard_01855_19144]
